saints.name: St. Maximilian Mary Kolbe
saints.title: Priest and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A Franciscan friar and apostle of Mary who gave his life in place of a condemned fellow prisoner at Auschwitz…
biography: Born in Poland in 1894, Maximilian Kolbe became a Conventual Franciscan and a tireless apostle of the Immaculate, founding the Militia Immaculatae and the vast friary and press of Niepokalanów, and serving for years as a missionary in Japan. His whole life was ordered to spreading devotion to the Mother of God.

Arrested by the Germans, he was imprisoned in the concentration camp of Auschwitz. When a prisoner was chosen at random to be starved to death in reprisal for an escape, Kolbe stepped forward to take the man's place; after two weeks in the starvation bunker he was killed by an injection of carbolic acid on 14 August 1941.
saints.knownFor: Offering his life to save another prisoner at Auschwitz.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. Maximilian Kolbe (vatican.va)
